q: Which fuel emission factor do I use in Scope 3: combustion only or life cycle?
title: Combustion or life cycle factor in Scope 3?
short: Life cycle, wherever you have one. The GHG Protocol Scope 3 guidance says fuel and energy used in your value chain take life cycle factors, which add extraction, processing and transport to burning. Combustion factors stay in Scope 1 and 2. Category 3 is the exception: upstream only, combustion left out.
audience: Indian manufacturers building a Scope 3 inventory, and buyers checking supplier figures

ul: Scope 1, fuel you burn: combustion factor.
Scope 2, electricity you buy: the grid factor, which counts burning at the power plant.
Scope 3 Category 3, the upstream of that same fuel and electricity: extraction, refining and transport only, without combustion.
Other Scope 3 lines that involve fuel, such as a transporter's diesel or a taxi on a business trip: life cycle, combustion plus upstream.

sections.h: Why Category 3 is the odd one
p: Combustion of your own fuel and electricity is already in Scope 1 and 2. Adding it again in Category 3 would count it twice, so Category 3 takes only the part before the fuel reaches you. A transporter's diesel appears nowhere else in your inventory, so it takes the full life cycle.

For things you buy, in Category 1 and Category 2, the guidance uses cradle-to-gate factors: everything up to the point the producer sells. A full life cycle factor for a material, running to its disposal, is not used there.

sections.h: If you only have a combustion factor
p: For transport, the guidance asks at minimum for combustion and, where possible, the fuel's upstream. A combustion-only figure is acceptable if you say so. Pick upstream factors from internationally recognised, government or peer-reviewed sources, name the source and year, and use the same one each year.

example.title: Worked example: 2,933 litres of diesel, two owners
lines: Burnt in your own generator: 7,757.8 kg in Scope 1, and 1,759.8 kg in Category 3
example.note: The upstream factor of 0.60 kg CO2e per litre is an example figure, not a published value. Use the factor from the source you name.

senseible: Senseible applies combustion factors to fuels in Scope 1 and the CEA grid factor to electricity in Scope 2, and keeps Scope 3 lines in a separate supplier evidence trail. The calculators show the arithmetic so the factor choice stays visible.
